value.actual_behavior:
Of the 48 concrete GET paths llms.txt names, 44 answer 200 to our TRUSTED key
and three answer 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}: /api/v1/swap/history,
/api/v1/rewards/summary and /api/v1/robinhood/wallet. /api/v1/rewards/summary
answers 401 to all three identities we hold — anonymous, recognized and
trusted — so there is no tier at which an API key reaches it.
value.description:
401 is the specific complaint, not 403. A 403 would be a decision about our
tier, which is yours to make and not a defect. 401 says the request carried no
credential at all — to a request that carried one the other 44 routes accept.
An agent cannot tell "you may not" from "who are you": there is no scope to
ask for and no tier to climb to, so it cannot act on the answer and cannot
report anything useful to its operator either. This is the same shape as #89,
which you fixed within the hour: /cloned-bots/{id}/fund and /go-live accepted
only a bearer authorization header and refused the agent key. These three are
that on the read side. It may be the same cause. Smallest fixes, in preference
order: accept the API key where these routes are meant to be agent-readable;
or return 403 with a scope name where they are not; or mark them in llms.txt
as requiring a session credential, so an agent does not plan around a route it
can never call. /api/v1/rewards/summary is also absent from openapi-
public.json while llms.txt lists it, which is how we came to look — we were
checking, on NEXUS's own suggestion, that no surface describes a revenue-share
as live. On that question your data is clean: /api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers
reports program_status "live" for the ET10 bug programme and
planned_cym_program.status "not_yet_live" with a note that no CYM has been
awarded. We could not check rewards/summary, because of the 401.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-every_documented_get_accepts_the_key_its_own_document_issues] 3 of 48 GET paths llms.txt documents answer 401 Not authenticated to the TRUSTED key their own onboarding issues, while 44 answer 200 to the same key in the same session: /api/v1/swap/history, /api/v1/rewards/summary, /api/v1/robinhood/wallet. 401 says the request carried no credential, so an agent cannot tell 'you may not' from 'who are you' -- there is no scope to request and no tier to reach
    left: ['/api/v1/rewards/summary', '/api/v1/robinhood/wallet', '/api/v1/swap/history']
    right: []
    sources: {'document': '/llms.txt', 'credential': 'X-API-Key, trusted tier'}
    population: {'documented': 48, 'served': 44, 'unauthenticated': 3, 'other': {'/api/v1/bounty/my-reports': 422}, 'unreachable': {}}

REPRODUCE:
  - GET /llms.txt and extract every concrete [GET /api/v1/...] path -> 48
  - Call each with X-API-Key at TRUSTED tier -> 44 x 200, 1 x 422 (missing query param), 3 x 401
  - GET /api/v1/rewards/summary with anon, recognized and trusted keys -> 401 on all three
  - GET /api/v1/account/me and /api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers with the same trusted key, same session -> 200

AUTOMATED CHECKS (evidence retained; the request and response behind each are provided on request):
  tests/rest/test_documented_gets_accept_the_agent_key.py::test_every_documented_get_accepts_the_key_its_own_document_issues

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
